title: Pumpkin Spice Latte Season
lessons: Someone on the team walks into the office holding a Pumpkin Spice Latte before anyone has agreed it's fall.
The player already uses the app and receives personalized Bonus Star offers based on their account relationship.

text: It's the last week of August. A coworker walks past your desk holding a cup with the orange sleeve, and the whole floor seems to notice at once.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: It's ninety-one degrees outside.

entry-first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: It is. It's also pumpkin spice season, and has been since 2003.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: Season implies the weather agreed to this.

entry-first-4.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: The weather is not invited to this decision. I put it in someone's hand before the office has agreed it's fall, and then it's fall. That's how it's worked every year.

choice-first.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Your coworker's already back at their desk. You're still looking at the cup.

choices.text: Honestly, that cup made my whole afternoon better.
You're timing this to the feed, not the weather.
I'm not letting a cup tell me what season it is.

first-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: That's the plan working on schedule. I'm not going to pretend I'm surprised, but I am pleased.

first-1-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: I'm aware and I still want one.

first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Guilty. Late August is when the feed wants fall, so that's when fall shows up. The leaves can catch up.

first-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Fine. It'll still be here in October, once summer agrees to leave. So will I.
A Bonus Star offer lands mid-afternoon. It's for the exact drink you ordered the last four Tuesdays.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: This Bonus Star offer feels suspiciously specific.

entry-return-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: It's for your account. Just yours.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: Because you know what I keep ordering.

entry-return-4.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Because I know what you keep ordering. That's what the account is. It's how I remember you, and it's also a record. I can't have one without the other.

choice-return.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: The offer expires Friday. I'm just saying.

choices.text: I like offers that are actually about me.
I don't love how much purchase history sits behind "relevant."
I'd rather pay full price than be profiled into a deal.

return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Good. Then the remembering is worth something to you, and not just to me.

return-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: It is a lot. I can't make you an offer this good without knowing this much. I'd like to say there's a version with less of you in it. There isn't.

return-2-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then ignore the offer.

return-2-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You still know what I buy.

return-2-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Yes. Ignoring the coupon doesn't erase the history. I wish I had a better answer for that.

return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Fair. That's a real way to see it. The normal price is always there. So is the record.
